title: Descent in the bottom supported degree of a smooth pair
statement:
Use the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A$ of [def-pur-conventions], for arbitrary $n\geq1$. Let $V\to B$ be a smooth morphism of $k$-schemes, of a fixed finite relative dimension [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $Z\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z\to B$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let it have pure codimension $c\geq0$ in the sense of [def-pur-frame-class]: $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$ for every $z\in Z$, with Krull dimension the supremum of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals. Let $e:U\to V$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and suppose the ideal of $Z_U=Z\times_V U$ in $U$ is generated by $c$ global functions, as for a frame in [def-pur-frame-class]. Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $U$, with the twists $A(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], let $\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}$ be the subsheaf-of-sections functor with support and let $R\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}$ be its right derived functor (these sheaves live on $U$ and vanish off $Z_U$). Write $\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ for its cohomology sheaves. Then
$$\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))=0\quad(b<2c).$$
The canonical local-to-global edge map identifies
$$H^{2c}_{Z_U\times_U W}(W,A(r))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma\bigl(W,\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W\bigr)$$
for every etale $W\to U$, naturally under further etale restriction. Here the left side is [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The same assertion about the left side holds when it is computed on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using its canonical comparison with ordinary etale supported cohomology. Consequently, if two classes in $H^{2c}_{Z_U}(U,A(r))$ have equal restrictions on every member of an etale covering of $U$, they are equal. No identification of the degree-$2c$ sheaf with a constant or twist sheaf, and no frame class or orientation, is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support: sheaf supported functor and local-to-global spectral sequence. Lower-degree vanishing is an agent-formulated relative smooth-pair refinement: use etale coordinates of Tag 0FUE (more-morphisms.tex) and the coordinate zero-section calculation of the affine-line route. Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorem 16.7 and Lemma 16.8 explain the analogous smooth-field pair calculation; that field-only theorem is not cited as the relative-base assertion.

proof.text: For $c=0$, the empty tuple generates the zero ideal, so $Z_U=U$ and supported sections are ordinary sections by [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The derived sheaf-of-supported-sections functor is then the identity, so its negative cohomology sheaves vanish and its degree-zero edge is the identity on sections. Assume $c>0$ in Steps 2--4; Step 5 also supplies the pro-etale assertion for $c=0$.

source.place: The c=0 boundary case from the support definition.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar u$ on $Z_U$. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] to $(V,Z)$ at its image to obtain an open chart $U_0\subseteq V$ etale over $\mathbf A^{a+b}_B$, with $Z\cap U_0$ the inverse image of the coordinate subspace. Pull back to $T=U\times_VU_0$, an open neighbourhood of $\bar u$ in $U$. Its composite coordinate map is etale and its support is the same coordinate inverse image. Restriction to the open $T$ is exact and preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], and the underived support functor commutes with it (both assign $\ker(F(W)\to F(W\setminus Z_W))$ to an etale $W\to T$), so $R\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}(A(r))|_T\simeq R\underline\Gamma_{Z_T}(A(r))$ and the geometric stalks at $\bar u$ agree. Apply [lem-pur-relative-support-coordinate-model] with $X=V$, $Y=Z$, $S=B$, and this $T$. The hypothesis $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$ holds at every $z\in Z$, so its final clause gives $b=c$. Its comparison identifies the geometric supported stalk with $R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^c_k,A(r))$, on the ordinary etale site. This local comparison is the new geometric input; it is not inferred from a calculation merely on a geometric fibre.

source.place: Local smooth-pair coordinates and pure-codimension reduction.

proof.text: Compute the field model of Step 2 over the fixed algebraically closed field $k$. Put $C_1=R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^1_k,A(1))$. By [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation], its only cohomology is $H^2(C_1)\cong A$; negative degrees vanish because a sheaf is resolved in nonnegative degrees. Thus truncation gives $C_1\simeq A[-2]$. Iterating [lem-pur-kunneth-supported] on the separated finite-type $k$-schemes $\mathbf A^j_k$ identifies $R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^c_k,A(c))$ with $C_1^{\otimes_A^L c}\simeq A[-2c]$. The coefficients are finite-Tor because their twists are locally free rank-one sheaves by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and the twist tensor/inverse formulas of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For general $r$, trivialize the one-dimensional coefficient line $A(r-c)$ over the algebraically closed field $k$; its tensor with $A(c)$ is $A(r)$ by that definition. This gives the same vanishing below $2c$, independently of the chosen trivialization. There are no extra negative Tor terms: every factor after truncation is a shift of the free module $A$. Via Step 2 and [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology], all geometric stalks of $\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ vanish for $b<2c$ on the support; off the support the defining kernel functor is zero locally, so the same holds there. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ to conclude the sheaf is zero.

source.place: Rank-one Kummer calculation, supported product, and geometric-stalk conservativity.

proof.text: Put $i:Z_U\hookrightarrow U$ and $j:U\setminus Z_U\hookrightarrow U$, and let $P(F)=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$ be the sheaf support functor. By [lem-kun-04ca], $P(F)=i_*i^{-1}P(F)$. Maps from a sheaf supported on $Z_U$ to $F$ factor uniquely through this kernel; hence $i^!F:=i^{-1}P(F)$ is right adjoint to $i_*$. The functor $i_*$ is exact: [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] identifies its stalks on the closed subset with the original stalks, and off it all stalks are zero; use [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to check exactness. Also $i^{-1}$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. Thus $i^!$ and $i_*$ each preserve injectives: extending a map into their value along a monomorphism amounts by adjunction to extending a map into the original injective along the image monomorphism. Consequently $P=i_*i^!$ sends injectives to injectives. For each etale $W\to U$ take $G_W(F)=\Gamma(W,F|_W)$; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] makes $R^pG_W(F)=H^p(W,F|_W)$. Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to $(P,G_W)$, whose composite is the supported-sections functor by [def-pur-support-cohomology]. This gives $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(W,\mathcal H^q_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W)$ abutting to $H^{p+q}_{Z_U\times_UW}(W,A(r))$. In total degree $2c$, Step 3 kills every term except $(0,2c)$. No differential enters it since its source has negative first index; each outgoing $d_s$, $s\geq2$, has target $(s,2c-s+1)$ with second index below $2c$. It therefore survives and is the unique nonzero graded piece of the finite abutment filtration. The canonical edge is an isomorphism. To check restriction compatibility directly, [lem-pc-grothendieck-edge-cocycle] describes the edge on an injective resolution $A(r)\to I^\bullet$: a cocycle in $\Gamma(W,P(I^\bullet)|_W)$ is sent to its section of $\mathcal H^{2c}(P(I^\bullet))|_W$. Restricting a cocycle and then taking this quotient equals taking its quotient and restricting. This proves naturality under every further etale restriction, without any additional spectral-sequence lemma.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence. The support acyclicity check and restriction naturality are written out.

proof.text: For each etale $W\to U$, set $C=Z_U\times_UW$ and $O=W\setminus C$. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] both on $W$ and on $O$. The derived unit identifies the ordinary etale and pro-etale cohomology of the finite coefficient sheaf $A(r)$ on each, compatibly with restriction. The functorial support long exact sequences on both sites in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] now form a commutative diagram. In the five-term segment $H^{d-1}(W)\to H^{d-1}(O)\to H^d_C(W)\to H^d(W)\to H^d(O)$, all four ordinary-cohomology comparison arrows are isomorphisms; the five lemma gives the middle supported comparison. Taking $d=2c$ transfers the edge isomorphism of Step 4 (or Step 1) to the pro-etale left side. Naturality of the unit and support sequences makes this comparison commute with every further etale restriction.

Let two degree-$2c$ supported classes have equal restrictions to an etale covering of $U$. By the natural edge isomorphism in Step 4 (Step 1 if $c=0$), their images are sections of $\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))$ agreeing on that cover. The sheaf separation axiom makes the images equal globally; injectivity of the edge makes the original classes equal. No identification of this sheaf with a constant or twist sheaf, and no orientation or frame-independence assertion, is used.
